newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Building bucks trend as NZ shares end lower.
newsitem.headline: FCL Building bucks trend as NZ shares end lower.

text.p: * Lower Wall Street, weaker bond market afflict shares
* Fletcher Building bucks trend with emergence of good buyer

"Yesterday's rally was probably more of a sigh of relief rally than anything else. Today it's back to reality and the offshore markets are probably dragging our market lower," said Duncan Rutherford at ANZ Securities.

He said policy details revealed by the National-New Zealand First coalition, which plans to spend an extra $5 billion over three years but defer tax cuts by a year, were well received by the market. However, there was lingering concern over the power NZ First leader Winston Peters will wield as Treasurer.
Brokers blamed the losses on a 71 point fall on Wall Street, which was down nearly 130 at one stage, and weaker U.S. and local bond markets.

Fletcher Paper and Lion Nathan were among the casualties, but Fletcher Building bucked the trend with a four cent rise to $4.25. Murray Rutherford at SBC Warburg said an active buyer had emerged in the stock, which was also seen benefiting from lower mortgage rates and increased infrastructural spending under the new government. -- Mark Trevelyan 64 4 471-4277
